done_when: Every review gets the '## Review rules' section of the repo's AGENTS.md, read from the default branch and placed outside the Forge-managed block, as rules the reviewer follows, the same way '## Known traps' reaches cold reads (reuse that reader). A repo without that section gets no extra text. The skill and the AGENTS.md template tell clients the section exists.

findings.body: The new rules block is appended only by `instructions()`. The client sign-off review builds its own prompt in `review.signoff()` (lines 438–446), and `run()` uses that prompt instead of calling `instructions()` (line 336). Thus `forge decision accept client-signoff` reviews a repo with `## Review rules` without passing those rules to the reviewer. Add the section to that review prompt as well.
findings.title: Not done: Every review gets the repo's Review rules

findings.body: This test claims to cover every review but exercises only `forge close` for a fix and a task. Add a repository-suite test that puts `## Review rules` on the default branch, runs `forge decision accept client-signoff`, and checks the prompt sent to Autoreview. It would fail on the current sign-off path.
findings.title: Not done: end-to-end client sign-off review rules test

why: A repo's own review rules, such as which tests a change needs, never reach Forge's review, because the reviewer treats repo files as evidence, not instructions; clients have to dismiss findings their own rules already settle
